text.arabic_uthmani: لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

words.gloss_range: emphatic future negation that places the first reaching clause under categorical denial
words.prose: {{ar:لَنْ}} ({{tr:lan}}) opens the ayah by denying material access before any material subject is named. Its governed mood makes the first reaching clause a categorical correction, and the verse shifts from ritual procedure into theological interpretation.

topics.headline: categorical denial before the material subjects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial is established before flesh or blood can appear as possible agents.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as an emphatic negation particle governing the following verb, and the opening clause is the negated verbal frame.

topics.headline: procedure becomes interpretation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the section turning from how the rite is performed to what the rite cannot accomplish.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the ayah opening as a doctrinal correction after prior ritual instruction.

words.gloss_range: negated reaching or attaining under the opening negator; the material subjects are allowed grammatical agency only as failed access
words.root_gloss_range: broad range of reaching, attaining, affecting, and obtaining benefit; locally used as the repeated test of what can or cannot reach God
words.prose: {{ar:يَنَالَ}} ({{tr:yanāla}}) places the act of reaching before the delayed flesh-and-blood subjects, so the failed action is heard first and the material agents arrive afterward. The root’s reach, attainment, and benefit range is retained as pressure, but locally it is narrowed by the negated clause and by the repeated-root pivot: material reaching fails here so that inward piety can be affirmed with the same verb later. The canonical active wording keeps flesh and blood as failed agents, while variant contrasts show how that agency could have been softened; the unusual direction also turns a root often used for what reaches people toward what could reach God. Even the repeated n sound binds the opening negator and verb into one compact denial.

topics.headline: negated verb before delayed material subjects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the failed reaching before the sentence identifies flesh and blood as the failed agents.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the divine name the object and the flesh-blood pair the delayed subject under the opening negator.

topics.headline: reach and attainment range under material denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial is not only about physical contact but about any material route of access, attainment, or benefit.
topics.reason: The broader attainment and benefit range is coherent, but the claim that every branch simply applies is narrowed by the local syntax: flesh and blood are failed subjects in a negated reaching frame.

topics.headline: variant readings test material agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical active wording keeps the material subjects visibly responsible for a failed attempt, while variants show how that agency could have been softened or regularized.
topics.reason: Accepted variants are useful as contrast, but they do not replace the canonical active verb with delayed material subjects.

topics.headline: usual reaching direction is inverted toward God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a root often used for what reaches people is turned here toward what could reach God, sharpening the ritual correction.
topics.reason: The supplied inter-ayah rows support an inversion of direction, especially with harm or good reaching people (3:120, 9:74, 9:120); the 22:15 note is kept only as structural backdrop, not as a same-root echo.

topics.headline: first half of the repeated reaching pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same reaching verb will be denied here and affirmed later, making the ayah argue through controlled repetition.
topics.reason: The first and second reaching clauses are attached as negation and adversative correction, so the repeated root is the local argumentative hinge.

topics.headline: negator and verb sound bound together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening denial landing as one compact sound unit before the material nouns appear.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation supports the already visible negator-plus-verb unit and adds a small auditory payoff.

words.gloss_range: the named divine object of failed material reaching, fixed before the delayed material subjects appear
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field centered on worshipful deity and proper divine reference, with derivational disputes adding reverence and exaltation pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is the explicit object of the first reaching verb. The proper name appears before the flesh-and-blood subjects, fixing the failed target as God Himself; worship and exaltation pressure intensify that named target, while local case still controls the role. A variant can illustrate how the role might reverse, but the canonical accusative keeps material offering as the failed actor, and the later repeated object position will redirect proper approach from material reaching to magnification.

topics.headline: named divine target before material agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the target of failed reaching is named before the material subjects are allowed to appear.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the divine proper name the direct object of the first reaching verb.

topics.headline: variant reverses the role map
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical case makes flesh and blood failed agents rather than making God the grammatical subject.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as apparatus, but the aligned local surface is accusative and functions as direct object.

topics.headline: divine-name derivation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proper name carries worship and exaltation pressure, while the local syntax still decides its object role.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute adds reverential pressure but does not alter the local grammatical role.

topics.headline: same divine object across failed and valid approaches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah holds the divine object constant while changing the valid mode of approach from material reaching to magnification.
topics.reason: The divine name appears in the first reaching frame and later in the magnification frame, producing an ordered local contrast.

words.gloss_range: the sacrificial animals’ concrete flesh, plural and possessed, acting as a failed material subject
words.root_gloss_range: flesh and bodily substance, with wider joining or welding pressure useful only as irony beside the failed connection to God
words.prose: {{ar:لُحُومُهَا}} ({{tr:luḥūmuhā}}) is the first material subject of the negated reaching verb, and its suffix keeps the prior sacrificial animals in view. The concrete flesh is plural and distributable, so the denial covers a class of sacrificial pieces rather than one token of meat. It also begins the flesh-and-blood material totality; the wider joining pressure of the root survives as irony, because the very bodily substance that might seem to connect the rite to God is denied that connection.

topics.headline: possessed flesh as failed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sacrificial animals’ flesh being given grammatical agency only so that agency can fail.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the subject of the negated reaching verb, and the suffix refers back to the sacrificial animals.

topics.headline: flesh and joining pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an irony: bodily flesh is the visible joined substance of the rite, yet it cannot join the offering to God.
topics.reason: The local noun selects concrete flesh; joining or welding pressure remains only as lexical irony, not as a replacement for the local sense.

topics.headline: broken plural makes material multiple
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the denial covering the class of sacrificial flesh pieces rather than one isolated piece of meat.
topics.reason: The broken plural morphology coheres with the material-pair argument.

topics.headline: first pole of the material totality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices flesh beginning a pair that will make the rejected material offering comprehensive.
topics.reason: The word is joined to blood as the two material subjects under the same negated reaching frame.

topics.headline: minor sound texture
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound note adds no distinct reader-facing payoff after the flesh-as-material-subject topic.
topics.reason: The retained material-subject and merism topics already carry the reader-facing value.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle that binds blood to flesh inside the same negated material field
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the blood term with the flesh term inside the same negated frame. Because it fuses visibly with the following negator, the second material element is added without restarting the argument.

topics.headline: blood coordinated into the same denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices blood being added to flesh as one material field under one denial, not as a separate claim.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the blood term as conjoined with the flesh term under the opening negated verb.

topics.headline: conjunction and negator fuse visibly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surface sequence adds blood with a renewed negative marker rather than by bare coordination alone.
topics.reason: The form-level row is supported by the adjacent conjunction and negator sequence.

words.gloss_range: renewed negator that explicitly extends the denial to blood as the second material subject
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) renews the denial for blood. It closes the loophole that the life-fluid of sacrifice might count differently from flesh, while still keeping both nouns inside one opening exclusion.

topics.headline: blood receives its own negative marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that blood is explicitly excluded, not merely implied under the earlier denial.
topics.reason: The particle reinforces the negation for the second conjoined subject inside the same clause.

words.gloss_range: the animals’ blood as vital sacrificial fluid, plural and possessed, completing the denied material pair
words.root_gloss_range: blood as vital fluid and blood-marked substance, with rare nominal distribution and contested image/substance pressure
words.prose: {{ar:دِمَآؤُهَا}} ({{tr:dimāʾuhā}}) is the second material subject, possessed by the same animals and explicitly negated. It completes the flesh-and-blood totality: even the charged life-fluid of slaughter, with its rare and marked root profile, is still material and cannot reach God. The wider blood-spilling discourse (2:30) sharpens the point by keeping blood in the realm of spilled material, not divine access.

topics.headline: possessed blood as conjoined failed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices blood receiving full grammatical participation so its failure is explicit.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as a conjoined nominative subject, and the suffix preserves the animal antecedent.

topics.headline: life-fluid pressure without divine access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even the most charged physical sign of slaughter remains unable to reach God.
topics.reason: The root and distribution evidence support blood as marked vital fluid, while the local negation keeps it within the failed material class.

topics.headline: blood discourse recalls spilling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the blood term against a wider Quranic discourse of spilling (2:30), which makes its denial of access more pointed.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give the concrete reference (2:30); locally the point is contrastive, not controlling the parse.

topics.headline: blood completes the material totality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the edible body and vital fluid together covering the whole sacrificial material field.
topics.reason: The flesh and blood nouns form the two subjects of one denied reaching frame.

topics.headline: minor glottal sound note
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound note adds no separate reader-facing value after the retained material and vital-fluid topics.
topics.reason: The retained blood-as-vital-fluid topic already carries the substantive payoff.

words.gloss_range: connector that opens the adversative correction while keeping it attached to the denial
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) starts the turn into correction and is read with the following adversative as a compact onset. It does not detach the next clause from the denial; it lets the positive alternative grow directly out of what flesh and blood cannot do.

topics.headline: attached turn from denial to correction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the correction arriving as a connected pivot, not as a new disconnected statement.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the following clause to the first clause by contrast.

topics.headline: surface onset fuses with the adversative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the correction signaled by a compact surface onset rather than a loose addition.
topics.reason: The row is a form-specific observation about the adjacent conjunction and adversative particle.

words.gloss_range: light adversative correction that turns from denied material access to the successful inward alternative
words.root_gloss_range: adversative and corrective particle field; locally a light corrective turn rather than a case-governing heavy particle
words.prose: {{ar:لَٰكِنْ}} ({{tr:lākin}}) is the ayah’s hinge: not flesh and blood, but protective piety. Its light form leaves the repeated reaching verb to carry the correction, so the structure stays lean while the argument reverses direction.

topics.headline: light adversative without case government
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the correction is syntactically lean, with the following verb carrying the assertion.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as an adversative particle, and the following clause remains verbal rather than governed by a heavy particle form.

topics.headline: restrictive hinge from material denial to inward affirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah replacing the failed material pair with one successful inward alternative.
topics.reason: The particle stands between the negated material clause and the positive reaching clause, creating the local replacement structure.

words.gloss_range: affirmed reaching with an attached divine object; the repeated root now gives successful agency to inward piety
words.root_gloss_range: broad range of reaching and attaining; locally repeated as the successful counterpart to the earlier failed material reaching
words.prose: {{ar:يَنَالُهُ}} ({{tr:yanāluhu}}) answers the first reaching verb with an affirmed form and an attached divine object. The target is the same, but the subject has changed: successful reaching belongs to the inward quality, and the repeated cadence lets the reversal be heard. Agreement and passive variants test the wording from the side, but the canonical active form keeps inward piety as the agent that reaches.

topics.headline: affirmed reaching with attached divine object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar itself reversing the first clause: negated subjunctive becomes affirmed indicative, while the divine object remains in view.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as indicative with an object suffix, and attachment evidence identifies that suffix as the object reached.

topics.headline: variants test agreement and agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical active wording keeps inward piety as the successful agent, even while variants show possible agreement or passive alternatives.
topics.reason: The variant rows are useful as contrast; the canonical surface is active, masculine, and followed by the abstract subject.

topics.headline: abstract subject succeeds where matter failed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reaching is not rejected absolutely; the successful agent is changed from material substance to inward disposition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the inward noun the subject of this reaching verb, preserving the root while transforming the successful condition.

topics.headline: second half of the reaching mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same verbal root returning with the opposite outcome, so the ayah teaches through repetition and reversal.
topics.reason: The local repetition of the reaching verb is concentrated inside the ayah and maps directly onto denial followed by affirmation.

words.gloss_range: definite protective piety as the sole successful subject that reaches God in place of flesh and blood
words.root_gloss_range: guarding and self-protection field that yields protective piety; locally the inward state that succeeds where material substances fail
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-taqwā}}) stands alone where two material nouns failed. The definite abstract noun is the successful subject of reaching; its protective root image makes the replacement sharper, because what reaches God is an inward guarding orientation, not the animal’s outer matter. The same-surah heart echo (22:32) locates that successful quality inwardly, so the replacement converges through grammar, shield image, and section movement.

topics.headline: definite inward quality as reaching agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah assigning agency to a recognized inward quality rather than to the sacrificed materials.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the subject of the successful reaching verb, and definiteness treats the quality as already recognized.

topics.headline: guarding image inside the abstract noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the successful inward quality is not vague piety but a guarding, self-protective orientation.
topics.reason: Dictionary evidence supports guarding and self-protection as the root field, and the local noun carries that abstracted force.

topics.headline: one abstract noun replaces two concrete plurals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural hierarchy: two concrete material nouns fail, then one inward abstract noun succeeds.
topics.reason: The local contrast moves from concrete plural subjects in the negated clause to a definite abstract subject in the affirmative clause.

topics.headline: same-surah heart echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sacrifice section turning inward by linking this successful quality with the hearts mentioned earlier (22:32).
topics.reason: The supplied rows give a concrete same-surah echo with 22:32, where the same quality is tied to hearts.

topics.headline: inward source of valid approach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s central replacement converging: grammar, protective image, and section movement all point away from fallen flesh toward inward response.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence and boundary rows support the same local conclusion: what reaches God is the inward quality, not the fallen animal matter.

words.gloss_range: source phrase assigning the inward quality to the addressed community rather than to the animals
words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) closes the correction by assigning source to the addressed community. Whether the phrase is heard with the reaching verb or with the inward quality, the origin remains the people themselves: the animals provide material and benefit, but the successful inward quality must come from the community.

topics.headline: community as source of what reaches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the valid reaching is sourced from the addressed people, not from the animal material.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the suffix as the complement of the source preposition, and the phrase closes the correction clause.

topics.headline: source can attach to quality or reaching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that either attachment keeps the same point: the human community is the source domain of the successful inward quality.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is locally source-marking whether read with the noun or the verb, so the payoff is stable.

words.gloss_range: bound manner/comparison particle forming a compact pointer back to the preceding correction
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) binds to the following demonstrative and turns the prior correction into a manner frame. The subjection clause is therefore read in the same logic: animals are made serviceable according to the principle just stated.

topics.headline: bound manner particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the next clause being tied to the preceding correction by manner, not merely sequence.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a prepositional comparison particle governed with the following demonstrative as part of the explanatory clause.

topics.headline: transition into purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from what reaches God to why animal subjection was arranged.
topics.reason: The particle begins the phrase that leads into the subjection and purpose clauses.

words.gloss_range: demonstrative pointer gathering the prior denial-and-correction into the basis for the subjection clause
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) points back to the whole denial-and-correction argument rather than to a visible object. Its marked demonstrative shape gives the hearer a distal, address-aware pointer, compressing the principle into a hinge so the purpose statement does not become a separate topic.

topics.headline: demonstrative gathers the prior argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the following subjection clause depending on the logic already established about material failure and inward success.
topics.reason: The demonstrative functions anaphorically inside the explanatory clause, pointing back to the preceding argument.

topics.headline: distal and addressee features in one pointer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pointer as marked and address-aware rather than as a bare connective.
topics.reason: The form-specific row adds demonstrative precision without changing the anaphoric function.

words.gloss_range: completed divine subjection of the sacrificial animals for human use and response
words.root_gloss_range: subjection, harnessing, and making serviceable, with a separate mockery branch that remains background rather than the local sense
words.prose: {{ar:سَخَّرَهَا}} ({{tr:sakhkharahā}}) resumes the same sacrificial animals and presents their serviceability as a completed divine act. The Form II harnessing sense is local; the mockery branch remains only background tension, while the repeated adjacent-ayah subjection frame (22:36) shows that the institution now receives its purpose. That same subjection language also places the animals within the broader pattern of God making creation serviceable.

topics.headline: animals subjected by completed divine act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals’ availability is God’s accomplished arrangement, not a material transfer to God.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect Form II verb with an attached animal object, and attachment evidence places it in the explanatory clause.

topics.headline: root tension narrowed to serviceability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices concrete harnessing pressure: the animals are made serviceable for response, while the mockery branch is not the local sense.
topics.reason: Dictionary evidence distinguishes subjection and mockery branches; the local Form II animal object selects subjection and harnessing.

topics.headline: prior-ayah and cosmic subjection frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sacrificial animals placed within a broader divine-subjection pattern, with the adjacent prior verse giving the immediate institution (22:36).
topics.reason: The supplied rows connect this Form II subjection to adjacent 22:36 and to broader subjection passages, while local syntax keeps the animals as the object.

words.gloss_range: benefactive phrase marking the addressed community as the recipients of the animals’ subjection
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) names the people as beneficiaries of the animals’ subjection. That role split is essential: the animals are for the community’s benefit, while reverent response is directed to God. The same addressed community also appears as source, beneficiary, and recipient of guidance, with the beneficiary frame repeated from the adjacent institution (22:36).

topics.headline: humans receive the subjection benefit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that animal serviceability benefits humans rather than carrying material value upward to God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the phrase as the beneficiary complement of the subjection verb.

topics.headline: one addressed community across source, benefit, and guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same community moving through source, benefit, and guidance roles across the ayah and adjacent verse (22:36).
topics.reason: The repeated second-person plural suffix and the 22:36 beneficiary frame keep the addressee stable.

words.gloss_range: purpose particle making magnification of God the stated telos of animal subjection
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) makes the next verb the purpose of subjection and governs it as a dependent subjunctive. Without this particle, subjection and magnification would sit side by side; with it, purpose and human action are fused, and the animals’ serviceability is explicitly for the community’s declaration of God’s greatness.

topics.headline: purpose particle attaches magnification to subjection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices animal subjection receiving its explicit telos: magnifying God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following clause as the purpose of the subjection clause.

topics.headline: purpose particle governs the following verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices purpose and human action fused into one grammatical unit.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as purposive and the following imperfect as governed by it.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive plural act of declaring God great as the communal purpose of the rite
words.root_gloss_range: greatness field spanning declaration of greatness and self-magnifying arrogance; locally selected as declaring God great
words.prose: {{ar:تُكَبِّرُوا۟}} ({{tr:tukabbirū}}) is the communal purpose: the addressed people declare God great in response to subjection and guidance. Form II makes this a declarative act, and the root contrast matters: the rite is not for self-display, but for directing greatness to God. The same root later names God as the great one (22:62), and the prior section’s gratitude is sharpened here into explicit magnification.

topics.headline: plural governed purpose act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the whole sacrificial arrangement aiming at a communal verbal response.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second-person plural subjunctive governed by the purpose particle, and attachment evidence links it to subjection.

topics.headline: declaring greatness rather than producing it
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that humans do not make God great; they declare the greatness that belongs to Him.
topics.reason: The Form II evidence and local direct object support declarative magnification.

topics.headline: greatness directed to God not self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root family’s contrast: proper greatness is declared for God, not claimed by the human performer, with a later same-surah attribute echo (22:62).
topics.reason: The arrogance branch is not the local sense, but it provides a valid contrast to the commanded declaration; 22:62 gives the same-surah attribute echo.

topics.headline: audible and section-level response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the named verbal response sharpening the prior section’s gratitude into explicit magnification.
topics.reason: The sound and boundary rows support the prominence of the purpose verb without changing its local meaning.

words.gloss_range: the repeated divine proper name as object of magnification, contrasting with the earlier failed reaching object
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field centered on worshipful deity and proper divine reference, now governed by the magnification verb
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) repeats the divine proper name as the object of magnification. Worship and exaltation pressure now belongs under the command to magnify, not under material access. The ayah thus holds God as the constant object across two approaches: material reaching fails, while guided declaration of greatness is the valid response.

topics.headline: repeated divine name under a new governor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the target of the purpose clause made explicit instead of reduced to a pronoun.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the repeated divine proper name the direct object of the magnification verb.

topics.headline: name field oriented into magnification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship and exaltation pressure now oriented into verbal magnification rather than material access.
topics.reason: The derivational field can enrich the divine-name object, but local grammar selects object of magnification.

topics.headline: same object contrasts invalid and valid approach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s controlled contrast: the same divine object is not reached by matter but is magnified by guided speech.
topics.reason: The two accusative divine-name occurrences are governed by different verbs, creating the local contrast between failed transfer and valid response.

words.gloss_range: basis preposition linking magnification to the guidance God has given
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) grounds the magnification in what God has guided the community to. Its spatial sense is narrowed into basis: the community declares God great upon the received ground of guidance, not as an unsupported slogan.

topics.headline: basis preposition for magnification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices magnification resting on completed guidance as its ground.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the preposition to the relative guidance clause, and the local meaning is causal or basis-oriented rather than merely spatial.

words.gloss_range: open relative object after the basis preposition, leaving the content of guidance expansive but governed
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) keeps the basis of magnification open while grammatically governed. It does not name one limited object of guidance; it lets the relative clause carry the full content of what has been given.

topics.headline: open relative object after the basis preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the guidance basis as both actual and expansive, not reduced to one named item.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a relative pronoun governed by the preceding preposition and completed by the following guidance verb.

topics.headline: relative phrase carries the whole basis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse compresses the content of guidance rather than listing it.
topics.reason: The relative construction leaves the object unnamed while keeping it syntactically recoverable through the following verb.

words.gloss_range: completed direct divine guidance to the addressed community, grounding their magnification as response
words.root_gloss_range: guiding, leading, way, gift, and sanctuary-offering branches; locally direct completed guidance with sacrificial-offering resonance
words.prose: {{ar:هَدَىٰكُمْ}} ({{tr:hadākum}}) presents guidance as already accomplished for the addressed community. The path-leading sense is local, while the gift and sacrificial-offering branches add resonance in a sacrifice ayah; magnification becomes response to received guidance, not a purchase of it. The same-surah guidance thread includes the nearby sacrifice framing (22:34) and broader references (22:16, 22:17, 22:24), so the clause lands as part of a local guidance pattern.

topics.headline: perfect guidance with communal object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the community magnifying God in response to guidance already given.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect verb with second-person plural object, and attachment evidence completes the relative clause.

topics.headline: direct divine guidance rather than negotiated exchange
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance as God’s direct completed act that grounds the purpose clause.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb with attached object presents direct guidance and resolves the basis phrase after the preposition and relative pronoun.

topics.headline: guidance and offering branches resonate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the guidance root resonating with sacrificial offering and gift fields while the local verb still means guiding.
topics.reason: The offering and gift branches are valid root pressure in a sacrifice context, but local grammar selects completed guidance to the community.

topics.headline: path pressure and same-surah guidance thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance as a route already received and as part of a same-surah thread including 22:34 and other references (22:16, 22:17, 22:24).
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete same-surah guidance references; locally they support the basis for magnification rather than changing the verb sense.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening a new singular imperative while keeping the final command joined to the purpose clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new imperative while keeping it joined to the preceding purpose clause. The addressee shifts from the community’s plural response to a singular command to announce good news.

topics.headline: conjunction introduces singular imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause boundary where communal magnification gives way to a singular prophetic announcement without breaking the ayah’s argument.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the final imperative clause as coordinated, and the following verb supplies the singular address shift.

words.gloss_range: singular intensive command to announce good news to the final recipient class
words.root_gloss_range: skin, human surface, and glad-tidings field; locally the intensive command to announce good news
words.prose: {{ar:بَشِّرِ}} ({{tr:bashshir}}) is the singular command that resolves the ayah into announced good news. It separates the Prophet’s role from the community’s magnification, governs the final recipient class directly, and lets the body-root field return as joyful response rather than sacrificial flesh. The repeated closing formula (22:34) brackets the sacrifice section while changing the recipient class.

topics.headline: singular addressee after communal purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah shifting from what the community does to what the Prophet is commanded to announce.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second-person masculine singular imperative, distinguishing it from the prior plural purpose verb.

topics.headline: announcement assigned to a defined class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final clause as a directed announcement, not general optimism.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following participial class the direct object of the imperative.

topics.headline: skin-joy and intensive delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices bodily response returning as joy caused by news, not as flesh or blood that reaches God.
topics.reason: The body-surface and glad-news root field is valid pressure, while the local Form II imperative selects intensive announcement.

topics.headline: same closing formula with new recipient class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sacrifice section bracketed by a repeated good-news command, with the recipient class changed from the earlier close (22:34).
topics.reason: The rows give the concrete 22:34 echo; locally the command form is repeated while the final recipient class changes.

words.gloss_range: definite active participial class of excellent actors who receive the closing good news
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, goodness, and excellence field; locally an active participial class of people characterized by excellent action
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ}} ({{tr:al-muḥsinīn}}) is the final recipient class and the ayah’s last word. Grammar makes them the direct object of the good-news command; morphology makes them recognized, continuing doers of excellence. The root range gathers beauty, goodness, and performative excellence, and the same-surah excellence field (22:58) helps the verse land on human quality of action rather than sacrificial matter.

topics.headline: definite participial object of the announcement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the good news aimed at a defined class of excellent actors, not at an unnamed audience.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word the accusative direct object of the final imperative, and definiteness marks a recognized class.

topics.headline: active participle of produced excellence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recipients characterized by ongoing excellent action, not by a single good deed or mere status.
topics.reason: The active participle and Form IV evidence support continuing excellence-agency as the local human profile.

topics.headline: beauty, goodness, and excellence converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final class carrying moral, aesthetic, and performative quality, matching the ayah’s rejection of mere material offering.
topics.reason: The root range coheres with the local active participle and does not conflict with the final recipient role.

topics.headline: ayah closes on excellent actors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s movement landing on excellent actors: material sacrifice denied, inward piety affirmed, magnification commanded, and excellence rewarded.
topics.reason: The final position, same-surah excellence field including 22:58, and structural row all support this as the closing human profile.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated reach verbs at words 2 and 8 hold the destination constant while flesh, blood, and taqwa exchange subject position across the not-but contrast.
baseline_models.mechanism: One predicate creates two transfer lanes. Material portions fail to attain God, while the worshipper's self-protective orientation does attain; acceptance is shifted from commodity to disposition.

activation_trace.role: Attainment and reaching supply the shared predicate whose repetition sorts what can arrive.
Literal meat supplies the first visible sacrificial substance excluded from Godward arrival.
Literal blood supplies the second visible sacrificial substance excluded from Godward arrival.
Putting oneself in protection makes taqwa an active inward stance and the positive subject of reaching.

changed_reading.before: God does not receive animal parts but receives piety.
changed_reading.after: The repeated reach-construction functions as a transfer filter: no material portion constitutes the Godward arrival, while the worshipper's protective self-positioning can.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Words 12, 14, and 18 form a purpose chain from making the animals serviceable, through magnifying God, to the guidance that warrants that response.
baseline_models.mechanism: Animal serviceability is purpose-bound rather than self-justifying. Enabled use is converted into an enlarged estimation of God because the enabling itself arrives within guidance.

activation_trace.role: Making a thing tractable and directing it to a purpose supplies the enabled-use stage of the chain.
Regarding something as great within the chest makes takbir a change of valuation, not merely a sound.
Gentle direction toward a way or truth supplies the prior guidance to which magnification responds.

changed_reading.before: Subjection, takbir, and guidance are three adjacent devotional ideas.
changed_reading.after: They form a causal sequence: divinely enabled use should terminate in a corrected estimation of God because the user has first been shown how to use the gift.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The final command at word 19 addresses the doers of beautiful or excellent action at word 20.
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing announcement opens joy specifically for a class defined by enacted excellence. The verse therefore ends with an ethical human outcome rather than with successful processing of sacrificial matter.

activation_trace.role: News that opens the face with joy supplies the promised announcement and its affective effect.
Beautiful, excellent, and beneficent action defines the recipients by practice rather than ritual possession.

changed_reading.before: The verse closes with generic good news for good people.
changed_reading.after: Its closing command identifies enacted excellence as the human endpoint of the sacrifice-and-guidance sequence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context assigns sacrificial matter a horizontal destination. Meat is apportioned as nourishment and explicitly delivered to other people, while taqwa alone occupies the Godward reach lane.

activation_trace.role: Delivery to another activates a directional reading of the repeated reach verbs and permits their destinations to diverge.
Meat as something fed or provisioned activates a social destination latent in the denied material subject.
Nourishing provision frames the animal as allocated sustenance rather than tribute needed by God.
Feeding another gives the material offering an explicit human addressee.
The repeated feeding command immediately before the focus ayah makes horizontal delivery the local outcome of slaughter.

structural_cues: 22:28 pairs eating from the animals with feeding the distressed poor.
22:36 repeats eating and feeding after the animals fall, immediately before 22:37.
22:37 then contrasts the failed reach of matter with the successful reach of taqwa.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit food recipients and the repeated reach contrast; I infer a redirection from vertical transfer to horizontal distribution. A live alternative is that the feeding commands and the reach denial are adjacent but independently motivated ritual rules.

changed_reading.before: Meat and blood are simply rejected as incapable of reaching God.
changed_reading.after: The meat is not discarded but reassigned: it reaches eaters and people in need, while the taqwa enacted through that routing is what reaches God.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier blood-like clot and flesh-like morsel stages place the same materials inside divine creation and transformation. The focus denial therefore limits matter's cultic destination without declaring embodiment valueless.

activation_trace.role: Literal flesh anchors the material whose value is being distinguished from its ability to arrive at God.
Literal blood anchors the second bodily material whose role is limited rather than despised.
The thick blood-like clot supplies an earlier life-stage in which blood imagery belongs to generative creation.
The chewed-looking piece of flesh supplies a bodily stage transformed toward completed life.

structural_cues: 22:5 sequences dust, drop, clot, morsel, birth, maturity, death, and revived earth.
22:37 denies a transfer function to flesh and blood but does not negate their created existence or human use.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies generative clot and flesh stages; I infer that they correct an anti-material reading of the focus contrast. A live alternative is that 22:5 serves resurrection proof only and does not qualify sacrificial valuation.

changed_reading.before: The spiritward element matters and bodily matter is worthless.
changed_reading.after: Bodily matter remains a divinely formed, transformable good; what is denied is its use as currency of divine need or acceptance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens with self-protection under destabilizing danger and later locates sacrificial taqwa in hearts. The focus's successful subject is thus an inward protective orientation tested under exposure, not an invisible substance detached from conduct.

activation_trace.role: Self-placement within protection anchors taqwa as an active orientation in the focus ayah.
Protective shielding frames the surah's opening command against the announced quake and harm.
The same self-protective orientation is explicitly tied to honoring ritual signs.
The heart supplies the stated locus from which sacrificial taqwa proceeds.

structural_cues: 22:1 places the first taqwa imperative against cosmic destabilization.
22:32 states that honoring the ritual signs proceeds from the taqwa of hearts.
22:37 repeats taqwa as the only subject that reaches God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies protection language, crisis, and an explicit heart locus; I infer a durable inward orientation that becomes visible in ritual handling. A live alternative is to keep taqwa as a broad obedience label without emphasizing protection.

changed_reading.before: Taqwa is a generic inward sincerity contrasted with outward ritual.
changed_reading.after: Taqwa is the heart's practiced self-guarding under danger and desire, made legible by how the worshipper handles God's signs and provisions.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same subjection formula first leads to feeding and gratitude, then later expands to the earth and ship moving under divine command. Human access to the animal is delegated usability inside a larger order, not autonomous mastery.

activation_trace.role: Purpose-directed tractability anchors the focus claim that the animals were made usable for people.
The immediately preceding subjection formula places animal use after feeding recipients and before gratitude.
Recognizing a benefit and its giver supplies the intended response to enabled use.
Earthly resources and the ship broaden purpose-directed serviceability beyond sacrificial animals.

structural_cues: 22:36 orders feeding before saying the animals were made serviceable and naming gratitude as the purpose.
22:37 changes the purpose wording from gratitude to magnifying God for guidance.
22:65 places terrestrial resources, sailing, and the held sky within the same divine ordering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated subjection formulas with gratitude, feeding, and cosmic command; I infer an entrusted-use relation. A live alternative is that subjection denotes benefit without carrying a stewardship norm beyond the stated commands.

changed_reading.before: God gives humans dominion over sacrificial animals so they can perform the rite.
changed_reading.after: God grants limited, purpose-bound usability within a wider created order; feeding, gratitude, and takbir prevent that access from becoming a claim of mastery.

context_deltas.mechanism: God is already named by greatness, while failure elsewhere is failure to measure God to His true measure. Takbir in the focus changes the worshipper's scale of valuation; neither the size nor quantity of an offering enlarges God.

activation_trace.role: Making something great in the chest anchors takbir as an internal recalibration of importance.
Intrinsic greatness and majesty identify God as already great rather than enlarged by worship.
Measure reaching its proper limit supplies the surah's explicit problem of estimating God rightly.

structural_cues: 22:30 and 22:32 use magnification for sanctities and ritual signs before the focus takbir.
22:62 names God as the High and Great.
22:74 diagnoses failure to measure God according to His true measure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies magnification, intrinsic divine greatness, and true measure; I infer that takbir corrects the worshipper's scale rather than adding magnitude to God. A live alternative is a narrower reading of takbir as prescribed praise after sacrifice.

changed_reading.before: Takbir is a verbal thanksgiving formula attached to completing sacrifice.
changed_reading.after: Takbir is guided scale-correction: the worshipper stops treating material magnitude as divine value and acknowledges the greatness God already has.

context_deltas.mechanism: The guidance root carries route, gentle gift, and sanctuary-bound offering branches. In a surah that guides people to good speech and a straight path while assigning rites, the focus can stage sacrifice as a response to God's prior gift and routing rather than as a purchase of guidance.

activation_trace.role: A gentle gift sent toward one held in affection activates guidance as prior divine giving.
An offering conveyed toward the sanctuary activates a reciprocal sacrificial shadow within the verbal guidance anchor.
Direction, course, and manner turn the repeated guidance to good speech and the praised path into route formation.
Sacrificial worship supplies the concrete rite in which the guidance and offering senses meet.
Gentle direction toward truth places the addressee on a straight guidance after rites are differentiated.

structural_cues: 22:24 twice directs people toward good speech and a praised path.
22:34 assigns each community a rite while centering one God and surrender.
22:67 again juxtaposes community-specific rite with straight guidance.
22:37 makes magnification a response to what God has guided.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the guidance, gift, offering, path, and rite branches; I supply the reciprocal arrow from God's prior routing to the worshipper's offering and takbir. A live alternative is ordinary gratitude for instruction with no activated gift-offering reciprocity.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper sacrifices and then thanks God for religious instruction.
changed_reading.after: The offering answers a prior movement from God: guidance is route and gift first, so sacrifice and takbir become responsive return rather than payment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier parallel announcement names the humble, then unfolds trembling hearts, patience, prayer, and spending; later public good is commanded. These cues give the focus's doers of excellence a behavioral profile beyond competent ritual performance.

activation_trace.role: Joy-opening news anchors the repeated announcement formula in the focus ayah.
Enacted excellence and beneficence anchor the class whose profile the context fills out.
The matching announcement to the humble creates a direct parallel recipient class.
Low, settled ground supplies a spatial image of unshowy receptivity for the announced recipients.
The outward flow of wealth makes humble inward response materially beneficial to others.
Recognized good approved by sound judgment supplies a public ethical horizon for excellence.

structural_cues: 22:34 ends with the same announcement command directed to the humble.
22:35 immediately describes their heart response, patience, prayer, and spending.
22:36 makes feeding others part of handling the sacrifice.
22:41 joins worship with alms, commanding recognized good, and restraining wrong.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a parallel announcement and an ensuing trait list; I infer that this list helps specify the focus's doers of excellence. A live alternative is that the humble and the doers of excellence are related but distinct recipient groups.

changed_reading.before: The doers of excellence are people who perform the sacrifice sincerely and well.
changed_reading.after: They are recognizable by a low, responsive heart whose patience, worship, spending, feeding, and public good carry the rite into social action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah names God as self-sufficient and contrasts Him with invoked objects unable to create or recover even a tiny creature's taking. The focus denial is therefore not failed access to a needy recipient; it reverses agency, since provision and capacity move from God toward creatures.

activation_trace.role: Attainment anchors the apparent transfer problem whose agency the wider surah reverses.
Self-sufficiency removes divine need as a possible reason for sacrificial matter to arrive.
Origination of created life exposes the invoked rivals' inability to produce even the smallest animal.
Extraction from another's grasp highlights the rivals' inability even to recover what is taken.

structural_cues: 22:64 places all that is in heavens and earth under the self-sufficient God.
22:65 presents God as the one making resources serviceable and holding the sky.
22:73 contrasts invoked objects' inability to create or retrieve with the focus's question of what reaches God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine self-sufficiency and the rivals' failed creation and retrieval; I infer that 22:37 denies divine dependency rather than reporting a physical delivery failure. A live alternative is that self-sufficiency is a general divine attribute without a specific sacrificial implication.

changed_reading.before: Physical offerings fail to bridge the distance to God, whereas piety succeeds.
changed_reading.after: God is not the needy endpoint of a supply chain at all; He supplies capacity and provision, and the only returning relation named is the worshipper's taqwa.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant d-m-y image branch rather than the surface sense of flowing blood. It remains anchored to the focus blood word and is activated by the nearby rejection of idols; render it only as an anti-spectacle lexical shadow, never as the primary lexical meaning.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The blood noun at word 6, evaluated through its packet-supplied d-m-y target, can carry a secondary image or figurine shadow.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant image or figurine branch lets displayed blood shadow a made cultic representation.
The worshipped idol supplies the nearby warning against material representation becoming a sacred substitute.

changed_reading.before: Blood is only sacrificial liquid that cannot reach God.
changed_reading.after: As a contained lexical shadow, displayed blood can also become an anti-icon: no material spectacle or cult-image can stand in for the taqwa that reaches.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading stretches flesh into the packet's kinship-and-loyalty branch, so it is social rather than anatomical and must remain qualified. It is still anchored to the focus flesh word and activated by community-specific rites and protected worship communities; downstream prose should present it as a critique of group possession, not as a replacement for literal meat.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The flesh noun at word 4 has a packet branch in which flesh names kinship and loyalty.

activation_trace.role: Flesh as kinship and loyalty supplies a social body whose claim to God can also be tested by the reach contrast.
Community as a gathered human type places the sacrifice within plural social bodies.
Places of prayer and worship broaden protected sacred space beyond a single communal enclosure.

changed_reading.before: Only animal flesh is denied Godward transfer.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, even the thick flesh of lineage, loyalty, or sectarian ownership does not reach God; community rite remains answerable to taqwa and enacted good.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is the most form-distant activation because it uses the packet's secondary h-d-d target for the focus guidance root. The direct demolition cue in 22:40 keeps the contrast inspectable, but prose must label it a sound-and-branch shadow: guidance is not being lexically redefined as demolition.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The guidance verb at word 18 is packet-mapped not only to h-d-y but also to an h-d-d target containing severe breakage.

activation_trace.role: The secondary severe-breakage branch casts a contained destructive shadow behind the focus guidance word.
The threatened bringing-down of worship buildings gives that shadow a concrete whole-surah counter-image.

changed_reading.before: Guidance simply supplies the reason for takbir.
changed_reading.after: As an explicitly contained counter-image, true guidance channels sacred force into magnification and protection rather than the demolition of other worship spaces.

strongest_changes: Sacrificial matter is horizontally delivered as food, while taqwa is the Godward arrival.
Taqwa becomes heart-located protective practice rather than generic invisible sincerity.
Animal subjection becomes entrusted use nested in feeding, gratitude, and a wider created order.
Takbir recalibrates the worshipper's measure of God instead of adding value through material quantity.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly rerouted the focus's material and directional vocabulary: clot and morsel kept embodiment dignified, feeding reassigned matter's recipient, heart cues located the accepted element, divine self-sufficiency reversed the supply chain, and split-root branches preserved anti-iconic, anti-communal, and anti-demolition shadows.
remaining_uncertainties: The horizontal-delivery model depends on how strongly the delivery-to-another branch of n-y-l should color the surface attainment construction.
The guidance-as-gift-and-offering reciprocity may be productive polysemy rather than an intended mechanism.
The d-m-y image, flesh-as-kinship, and h-d-d demolition readings are deliberately exploratory and must not displace the surface syntax.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Material contact is denied; guarded orientation reaches.** Repeated `ن ي ل B001/B002` contrasts what attains or is brought within reach; `ل ح م B001` flesh and `د م و B001` blood are negated, while `و ق ي B002` inward protective caution is affirmed. I infer that the material rite is a carrier whose intended endpoint is transformed agency, not divine consumption. Sacrifice reads as successful when its guarding posture reaches God relationally.
2. **Subjection should produce magnification, not ownership.** `س خ ر B001` is bringing under command for a purpose; `ك ب ر B003` regarding as great; `ه د ي B001` guidance; `ح س ن B002` beneficent good action. I infer that human control over animals is derivative guidance and must return as praise and beneficence. *Taskhīr* therefore reads as entrusted means whose moral output is gratitude, not autonomous domination.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:65's held sky and moving ship expanded the same distinction: material means serve human life, but their governing restraint remains divine compassion.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The rite's material carrier is not its transmitted value.** Repeated fixed `يَنَال` activates `ن ي ل:B001` (attaining or reaching), while `لُحُوم` and `دِمَاء` activate `ل ح م:B001` and `د م و:B001`. Their reaching is negated and replaced by `و ق ي:B002` in `ٱلتَّقْوَى`. `22:36` supplied naming, slaughter, eating, and feeding. The packet supplies material process and explicit correction; I infer that those acts convey inward guardedness only when they instantiate its social purpose. The ayah prevents flesh and blood from being read as substances transferred to God.
2. **Guidance redirects magnification away from the self.** Fixed `سَخَّرَهَا` uses `س خ ر:B001`, `لِتُكَبِّرُوا` activates `ك ب ر:B003` (regarding something as great), and `هَدَاكُم` uses `ه د ي:B001`. Because humans have been granted command over powerful animals, I infer a risk of self-magnification that the purpose clause reverses. Control should terminate in magnifying the guide and in `ح س ن:B002` (beneficent action), not the controller.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `22:38-40` unexpectedly extend the issue of rightly directed power from animal control to social defense. Magnification after guidance is corrected by protection of trust and multiple worship spaces, not self-aggrandizement.

baseline.text: Onların ne etleri ne de kanları Allah'a ulaşır; O'na sizden ulaşan, Allah'a karşı gelmekten sakınmanızdır. Sizi doğru yola ilettiği için Allah'ı yüceltesiniz diye onları hizmetinize verdi. İyilik yapanları müjdele.

findings.text: Allah'a ulaşan şey et ve kan değil, maddi taşıyıcıyı yönlendiren koruyucu sakınmadır.
Hayvanların insanlara boyun eğdirilmesi sahiplenmeyi büyütmek için değil, doğru yola ileten Allah'ı yüceltmek içindir.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It links guidance from God with the lasting outcome of the home, supporting the focus's attribution of guidance to God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Divine acceptance of repentance does not add a specific relation to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It contrasts those astray from God's path with the rightly guided, reinforcing the focus's emphasis on received guidance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It affirms revealed truth while noting widespread unbelief, a broad counterpoint to grateful acceptance of guidance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A community guides and acts justly by truth, extending divine guidance into communal conduct.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The prophetic command to taqwa and obedience supports the focus's devotional orientation without its sacrificial setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It gives gardens of bliss to the God-conscious, extending the focus's taqwa theme into its promised outcome.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It names the Safa and Marwah as God's ritual markers within Hajj, supplying the wider sanctuary-rite setting for the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands completion of Hajj and Umrah for God and prescribes the accessible sacrificial offering when prevented.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: After completing Hajj rites, pilgrims are commanded to remember God intensely, paralleling the focus's call to magnify Him.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It joins the appointed days of remembrance with taqwa at the close of pilgrimage observances.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It protects God's ritual markers, the sacred month, and marked sacrificial animals, directly framing their sanctity.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It states that God accepts only from the God-conscious, the clearest direct parallel to the focus's claim that taqwa, not animal matter, reaches Him.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its Hajj expiation requires a livestock offering reaching the Ka'bah, closely connecting animal sacrifice, destination, and accountability.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies the Ka'bah, sacred month, sacrificial animals, and garlands as God-established supports of the sanctuary order.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands eating what God's name was pronounced over, linking animal provision to conscious devotion to God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It prohibits eating animals not named for God, making divine orientation rather than mere flesh decisive for consumption.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It condemns assigning shares of crops and livestock between God and alleged partners, a direct corrective to misconstrued offerings.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly dedicates prayer, sacrifice, life, and death wholly to God, giving the governing purpose of the focus's ritual act.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands eating God's lawful good provision and thanking Him, matching the focus's use of subjected animals in grateful worship.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly commands God's name over provided grazing livestock, then eating and feeding the poor, immediately completing the sacrifice-and-provision logic.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It continues the Hajj sequence through fulfillment of vows and circumambulation, providing the ritual frame around the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands reverence for God's sanctities and avoidance of idolatry, supplying the devotional boundary for the sacrifice passage.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It affirms that every community has an appointed rite, extending the focus's teaching beyond one sacrificial instance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The ransom of Ishmael with a great sacrifice supplies a major Qur'anic instance of an animal offering, though it does not state the focus's taqwa criterion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly joins prayer to the Lord with sacrifice, expressing the God-directed intention that the focus makes explicit.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It permits what trained animals catch when God's name is mentioned and ends with taqwa, directly joining animal use, divine naming, and reverence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands eating God's lawful good provision while fearing Him, a general counterpart to the focus's grateful use of animals.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It rejects invented consecrations of particular animals, clarifying that animal ritual status cannot be fabricated apart from God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It criticizes fabricated restrictions on livestock and false claims about mentioning God's name over them, a direct distortion of the focus's devotional order.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It presents livestock as divinely created for human benefit, warmth, and food, providing the material-provision side of the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It calls livestock a lesson and names drink, benefits, and food from them, extending the focus's account of animal provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies livestock as a divine creation made available for human possession, introducing a close parallel to the focus's subjected animals.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It states that God subjected livestock so people may ride some and eat some, nearly restating the focus's provision logic.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It completes the livestock sequence with benefits, drink, and the question of gratitude, directly echoing the focus's thankful magnification.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It says God made livestock for people to ride and eat, a concise parallel to divinely ordered animal benefit.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies livestock among the created means of travel, supporting the focus's broader language of divinely subjected creatures.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands remembrance and praise of the One who subjected transport, closely paralleling the focus's magnification after subjection.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 (22:19-37) - Marked Animal Bodies Become Shared Provision
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Consecrated bodies pass through naming, alignment, collapse, distribution, and a final separation of material from moral reach.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sacrifice is a conversion chain rather than a single act: inward trembling organizes the body, slaughter reorganizes ownership, and piety travels where matter cannot.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Piety Reaches Beyond Flesh and Blood
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Flesh and blood stop at the material boundary, while protected moral orientation reaches its intended destination.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: reaching and attaining `quranic:root_001572:B001/m01`; flesh `quranic:root_001348:B001/m01`; blood `quranic:root_000490:B001/m01`; piety as protection `quranic:root_001677:B002/m01`; doing good `quranic:root_000323:B002/m01`

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The rite distinguishes transportable moral relation from non-transportable matter. Flesh and blood remain within the economy of bodies; piety is the element that crosses the vertical relation to God.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili söz öbeği, kişinin bir şeye ulaşıp onu elde etmesini açıkça bildirir; iyiliği elde etme ve elle alınan şey açıklamaları da bu çekirdeğin örnekleridir. Bu nedenle dalın ulaşma ve elde etme çerçevesi kanıtla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal, kişinin kendisinin bir şeyi elde etmesini anlatır; başkasına verme ve bir davranışın uygunluğunu değerlendirme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.
